candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is fibroadenoma, which is a biphasic tumor with both fibrous stroma and epithelial/glandular elements. Fibroma denotes a purely fibrous neoplasm without the adenomatous component, making it an incompatible subtype despite overlapping fibrous features.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Fibroma is a benign fibrous tumor but lacks the adenomatous (epithelial glandular) component required for fibroadenoma; it is a related but distinct entity

candidate_relations.reason: Adding the anal anatomic qualifier to fibroma does not transform it into a fibroadenoma. The reference requires a biphasic fibroepithelial neoplasm; anal fibroma remains a purely fibrous lesion and is therefore an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Anal fibroma specifies location and fibrous nature but still lacks the adenomatous component of fibroadenoma; anatomic qualifier does not resolve the missing epithelial component

case_quality_flags: Fibroadenoma of the anal canal is an exceptionally rare diagnosis; the clinical and gross pathology description (firm, gray-white, encapsulated, 20-year slow growth) is more consistent with a fibrous/fibroepithelial lesion, but the reference diagnosis of fibroadenoma requires histologic confirmation of glandular elements not explicitly described in the record.
